answer: Reputation-Weighted Routing Share: each identity's task inflow is capped by a moving average of its completed work, so a fresh clone starts near zero routing regardless of how many it spawns. An attacker must run each clone through the slow warm-up, paying full compute and time per identity before it earns any sable volume. Honest operators haven't a shortcut either, but their accumulated history compounds. The cost curve rises sharply per parallel identity and rewards depth over breadth, making juniper-scale sybil farms uneconomic.
